dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Good afternoon, Kevin. My name is Adriana Morales. I am calling for my mother, she is very old and she lives alone, and I am calling about the water in front of her house.
It is 477 Dixon Street, in the North End. Four seven seven.
Four seventy-seven Dixon. Got it. And what's going on there?

There is a grate at the curb, for the storm drain. It has sunk down, lower than the street, you understand? So when the rain comes, the water goes everywhere except down the grate. After the nor'easter that ended Saturday, there was a big pool in front of her walk. It is Monday and still there is a puddle.
Yeah, that'll happen after a storm like that. Sunk grate, so it's kind of dipped below the pavement. Let me jot that down. Is the water coming up onto the property or just sitting in the street?

Just one moment, please. I am making a little drawing, on the back of a receipt, so I explain it well. [pause] Okay. The water sits in the street and along the curb, and then it goes toward her driveway. Not inside the house, thank God. But it is a nuisance, she must walk through it to get to the mailbox.
Understood. Sunk grate, water pooling at the curb and running toward the driveway, not in the house. Has anyone called about this before?

Yes. I called last year, I think it was the autumn. A person told me that Dixon Street is a state road, and so it is not for the city. That the state must fix it. Nobody told me who at the state, or what number. So I did nothing, and now the grate is still the same.

Okay. Yeah, some of the bigger roads up that way are state-maintained, so that could've been the case. I don't want to just tell you the same thing again though. Let me put this in as a request so somebody from our side looks at it and figures out whose grate it is. If it's the state's, we can point you to the right office.
That would be very kind. It is a little annoying, to be sent from one office to another, you know. My mother is eighty-something, she cannot do this.

No, I hear you. Alright, I've got four seventy-seven Dixon, sunk storm drain grate at the curb, water not draining, past call said state road. Anything else I should note, like which side of the driveway?
It is on the left side, if you are looking at the house from the street. Just before her driveway starts.
Left side, before the driveway. Perfect. Best number to reach you?

It is four-zero-one, five-five-five, zero-one-eight-nine. And please, I ask that you call me back when it is done, or when you know whose it is. Not my mother, she does not hear well on the telephone.
Zero-one-eight-nine, got it. I'll note to call Adriana back, not your mom. Might take a few days with all the storm cleanup, but somebody will get back to you.
Thank you, Kevin. I appreciate it. Have a good afternoon.
You too, Ms. Morales. Take care.
